title: Entangling capability of coherently controlled quantum processes
authors: Beyza Aslanbaş, Bedirhan Alkan, Göktuğ Karpat
abstract: We analytically characterize entanglement generation by two paradigmatic coherently controlled quantum processes, the quantum switch and time-flip. Retaining rather than measuring or discarding the control, we treat the control and target as the bipartite system and assume pure product inputs, so that any output entanglement reflects the entangling capability of the process. For the switch of qubit unitaries, we derive exact expressions for entanglement, together with a geometric characterization and a coherence-entanglement conservation relation. We then extend our analysis to binary random unitary, Pauli, amplitude damping, and generalized amplitude damping channels. We prove that switch of channels commuting under composition cannot entangle a separable input. Yet maximal entanglement is possible even with dissipation, e.g., an entanglement-breaking damping channel switched with a bit-flip can transform a product input into a maximally entangled state. For two generalized amplitude damping channels, a common stationary state prevents entanglement, while different stationary populations can enable it. We present an analogous study for the time-flip of unitary and binary random unitary channels. Our findings provide a systematic analysis of how much entanglement can be generated by coherent control of channel order or input-output direction.
summary: This paper systematically analyzes the entanglement generated by coherently controlling quantum processes, specifically the quantum switch and the time-flip. By treating the control and target as a bipartite system, the authors derive conditions under which entanglement is generated, even when dissipation is present. The findings offer a deep, analytical understanding of how channel order and directionality can be harnessed to manipulate quantum correlations.
main_problem: The paper aims to analytically characterize the entanglement generation capability of two key coherently controlled quantum processes: the quantum switch and the quantum time-flip.
main_result: The entanglement generated depends critically on the coherence of the control process and the distinguishability of the ordered evolutions; maximal entanglement can persist even in the presence of dissipation.
method: The analysis involves treating the control and target as a bipartite system, deriving exact expressions for entanglement (concurrence) for unitary channels, and extending the analysis to various dissipative channels.
model_or_system: The model uses a bipartite system consisting of a control qubit and a target system, where processes are modeled by quantum channels (supermaps). The processes analyzed are the quantum switch (combining two channels) and the quantum time-flip (reversing input-output direction).
key_observables: Entanglement (quantified by concurrence), coherence-entanglement conservation relation, and stationary states of damping channels.
important_parameters: The distinguishability overlap parameter $s$, and the parameters governing the specific damping channels ($\gamma_1, \gamma_2, p_1, p_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes pure product inputs and crucially retains the control system rather than measuring or discarding it.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the quantum switch first, deriving general principles and specific results for unitaries and dissipative channels, followed by an analogous study for the quantum time-flip.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, analytical framework for quantifying how entanglement can be engineered by controlling the order or direction of quantum operations, which is fundamental to quantum information processing.

Density plots of the maximal concurrence for switch of two unitary channels, Cmax(U, V ), as a function of the rota- tion angles θU and θV for four different relative angles between the rotation axes. Here, the white point and curves highlight the contours on which the concurrence has constant value.

Figure 2. Density plots of the maximal concurrence generated via quantum switch of two binary random unitary channels. (a) Dependence of concurrence on the noise parameters p and q for t = 1/2 and (b) on the parameter pq and the unitary parameter t. The white contours indicate the parameter val- ues corresponding to Cmax = 0.20, 0.50, and 0.80.

Figure 3. Density plots of the concurrence generated by the switch for the two-parameter family of Pauli channels P and a unitary channel. The physically valid parameter region sat- isfies px +pz ≤1 and px, pz ≥0. (a) Maximal concurrence for the Hadamard-Pauli switch. The dashed white line px = pz marks the nonentangling condition. (b) Haar-averaged con- currence for the switch of unitary and Pauli channels, with U and |ψ⟩sampled independently according to the Haar mea- sure and the control fixed to the maximally coherent state.

Figure 4. Density plots of the concurrence generated by the switch of the amplitude damping Aγ and unitary channels, for the maximally coherent control state and the real target input |ψ(ϑ)⟩= cos(ϑ/2) |0⟩+ sin(ϑ/2) |1⟩. (a) Concurrence for the quantum switch of bit-flip and amplitude damping channels. (b) Haar-averaged concurrence for the switch of unitary and amplitude damping channels, obtained by averaging over U while keeping the control and target fixed.

Figure 5. Density plots of the concurrence generated by the switch of two generalized amplitude damping channels, Gγ1,p1 and Gγ2,p2, for the product input |+⟩C |+⟩T . (a) Both chan- nels are fully relaxing, i.e., γ1 = γ2 = 1. The dashed diagonal marks p1 = p2, for which the channels commute under com- position and the switched output is separable. (b) The first stationary population is fixed at p1 = 1, while the channels have a common damping strength, γ1 = γ2 = γ. The thicker solid white curves are the C = 0 boundaries.
